newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee tumbles in correction but support cit.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee tumbles in correction but support cit.

text.p: Coffee's staggering rally turned sour on Monday as prices erased a big chunk of their recent gains in a speculative liquidation.
But the losses bore the hallmarks of a technical correction as buyers returned at the lows lifting benchmark contracts to a more stimulating close, traders said.

"People thought there would be quite a sell-off in New York. But suddenly it has taken off again," said one trader adding that London's slump to a session low of $1,445 on March came in anticipation of wider losses in New York.
"This shows how fickle this market is," he added. "New York got so overbought last week that people thought there was going to be more of a reaction today."
March robusta dropped $43 to $1,475 at the close after being bid up to $1,485 by profit takers, represented by traders that sold March around $1,600.
Traders said strong fundamentals, including recent expectations that the Brazilian crop will be smaller this year, were likely to fuel prices in the near term.
"If what we think the Brazilian crop is going to be is true then 137 (cents on CSCE coffee) will look quite cheap," said one.
Turnover was a robust 8,278 lots, mostly in outright deals. Structure trading was subdued but March/May was quoted at level.
The Colombian port strike was resolved on Friday but exports are still threatened by a possible truckers' strike and a backlog of coffee shipments.
About 120 truck drivers were holding coffee cargoes slated for shipment from the main Pacific coast of Buenaventura demanding compensation for the time lost during the nine-day dockers' strike.
Another setback for supplies was torrential rains in key Colombian coffee regions over the past three weeks which was delaying the flowering period.
New York's March coffee bounced from a low of 133.50 cents a lb as local buying lifted the market after a round of profit taking.
In London, any further downside moves will be aimed to fill a chart gap between $1,424 and $1,390. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom 44-171-542 8072
